1. NOTE LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: mix is declared in a reservoir channel, not a tube
   line 41:  reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=mix_liquid, volume=500)
   Line 41 declares 500 ul of mix in channel A1 of NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL (slot 4,
     load name nest_12_reservoir_15ml). The request (PCR setup) puts its reagents in tubes,
     or at a temperature, and a reservoir channel is neither: 500 ul spread over the channel
     is 1.7 mm deep, open to the air and at room temperature, so it warms and evaporates
     while the run goes on, and the tip may not reach it.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Put mix in a tube on the block (a tube rack, or a temperature module with a tube
     block), not in a reservoir channel.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1

labware.title: mix is declared in a reservoir channel, not a tube
labware.explanation: Line 41 declares 500 ul of mix in channel A1 of NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL (slot 4, load name nest_12_reservoir_15ml). labware.fix: Put mix in a tube on the block (a tube rack, or a temperature module with a tube block), not in a reservoir channel.

protocol.py: 4 biology problems (2 errors, 2 notes).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 57:  p300.aspirate(50, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 57 the p300_single_gen2 draws 50 ul from mix (well A1 in slot 4) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 150 ul, which in this NEST 12
   Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.75 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it once, after 7 times in the liquid; 50 ul of air in all). The simulator
   does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 1 well filled from these draws got
   air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 1 other well: well A8 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [033bd0835316]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A2 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 63:  p300.aspirate(42, reservoir["A2"])
   At line 63 the p300_single_gen2 draws 42 ul from water (well A2 in slot 4) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 190 ul, which in this NEST 12
   Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 3 times, after 5 times in the liquid; 126 ul of air in all). The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 3 wells filled from these
   draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A2 in slot 4.
   Also reached 3 other wells: wells A6, A7 and A8 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [e7d42aadd300]

3. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 7 wells of mix with a sample
   line 58:  p300.dispense(50, plate[dest_name])
   At line 58 the robot starts putting mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt
   (slot 3), and 7 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds
   the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in
   slot 3.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 3.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 50 ul of mix and 8 ul of water in place of the
   template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [e61443207c28]

4. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 7 wells never mixed after template 1, template 2, template 3,
template 4 and 3 more went in (8 to 14% of the well)
   line 71:  p20.dispense(8, plate[dest_name])
   At line 71 the robot added template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 3 more to
   wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 3, which already held mix and water (this
   line did it 7 times). The addition was 8 to 14% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 3 after line 71: `mix_after=(5, 46
   to 80)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 46 to 80, well)`, with the volume about 80%
   of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [37f2fec64749]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 57 the p300_single_gen2 draws 50 ul from mix (well A1 in slot 4) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 150 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.75 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it once, after 7 times in the liquid; 50 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 1 well filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.explanation: At line 63 the p300_single_gen2 draws 42 ul from water (well A2 in slot 4) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 190 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 3 times, after 5 times in the liquid; 126 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 3 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.title: No no-template control: 7 wells of mix with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 58 the robot starts putting mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 3), and 7 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 50 ul of mix and 8 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 7 wells never mixed after template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 3 more went in (8 to 14% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 71 the robot added template 1, template 2, template 3, template 4 and 3 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 3, which already held mix and water (this line did it 7 times). The addition was 8 to 14% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 3 after line 71: `mix_after=(5, 46 to 80)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 46 to 80, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
